answer: Each identity registers a ledge mount, a juniper bob on filed thread, and an 85-credit bond. Each epoch it files thread length and time for 20 swings. Auditors recompute the period from the public pendulum table and reject deviation over 2 percent. Fees start at 41 credits, rising 3 per mount, so the 1000th pays 3038; 1000 false identities pay 1539500 and lock 85000, while an honest identity pays 41 and recovers its bond after a clean epoch. A rented-pendulum ring fails because a reused thread or juniper bob serial sits in the registry and its period matches the ledge mount, so both burn.
